anchor.quote: Your brain does not receive the world. It generates the world

claims.rationale: Predictive-processing literature models perception as inference, but the absolute claim that the brain generates rather than receives the world omits model limits, conditions, measures, and a traceable source.

legacy.quote: "Your brain does not receive the world. It generates the world"
legacy.note: Neural tissue is made the producer of experienced reality, but the same matter-first thesis recurs throughout the post.

anchor.quote: corrects its own hallucination against the resistance of the body

claims.rationale: Calling perception the brain's corrected hallucination asserts a broad causal mechanism without defining the measured phenomenon, conditions, population, uncertainty, or source.

legacy.quote: "corrects its own hallucination against the resistance of the body"
legacy.note: Neural machinery is made the author and corrector of experience; later matter-first formulations repeat the claim.

anchor.quote: the free energy principle, and it governs every system

claims.rationale: The free-energy formalism does not by itself establish that one principle governs every persistent system; the universal mapping omits required boundary, generative-model, and evidentiary assumptions.

legacy.quote: "the free energy principle, and it governs every system"
legacy.note: Friston's framework is promoted to a universal law, but L57 repeats the universalization several times.

anchor.quote: Karl Friston did not invent it. He described it

claims.rationale: The sentence converts a philosophical stance about natural principles into a historical fact about Friston without a quotation, source, or distinction between formulation and phenomenon.

legacy.quote: "Karl Friston did not invent it. He described it"
legacy.note: The metaphysical claim that the theory pre-existed its formulation is presented as history rather than interpretation.

anchor.quote: Tycho Brahe described the Martian orbit

claims.rationale: Tycho supplied exceptionally precise Mars observations and a geoheliocentric model; Kepler used those data to derive the elliptical Martian orbit, so the parallel overassigns the orbital description to Tycho.

legacy.quote: "Tycho Brahe described the Martian orbit"
legacy.note: Accurate historical reference to the house tradition's situated observational astronomer; it is illustrative rather than proof.

anchor.quote: A Markov blanket separates internal states from external states

claims.rationale: A Markov blanket conditionally separates internal from external states through a boundary set in the standard formal definition; that separation is the article's structural spine and has standard mathematical provenance.

legacy.quote: "A Markov blanket separates internal states from external states"
legacy.note: Conditional separation is the post's boundary grammar; removing it collapses the nested-boundary argument.

anchor.quote: Your skin is one. Your cell membrane is one.

claims.rationale: Skin and cell membranes can participate in modeled biological boundaries, but calling each a literal Markov blanket omits the required state partition, conditional independences, variables, and source.

legacy.quote: "Your skin is one. Your cell membrane is one."
legacy.note: Organismal and cellular boundaries are called literal Markov blankets, then the nested-boundary claim is immediately repeated.

anchor.quote: This is the Hermetic Principle of Correspondence operating at neurological scale

claims.rationale: The post combines a named Hermetic teaching with a neurological Markov-blanket model without separately passing the ingredients, showing the transformation, or declaring Noesis authorship.

legacy.quote: "This is the Hermetic Principle of Correspondence operating at neurological scale"
legacy.note: The Hermetic correspondence is named and operated as house cosmology.

anchor.quote: the same blanket that separates self from world

claims.rationale: The formal Markov-blanket relation is silently extended from statistical state partitions to organism, cell, and cosmological observer boundaries without constructing equivalent variables or conditional independences.

legacy.quote: "the same blanket that separates self from world"
legacy.note: A model-dependent statistical boundary is silently upgraded across scales, but adjacent sentences carry the same claim.

anchor.quote: the only way to minimize surprise across nested boundaries

claims.rationale: No theorem or evidence shows that the stated nested-boundary pattern is the only way to minimize surprise; the exclusivity claim is not entailed by the free-energy formalism.

legacy.quote: "the only way to minimize surprise across nested boundaries"
legacy.note: The exclusive universal mechanism is asserted without qualification and is repeated at L55, L57, and L65.

anchor.quote: I held my hand before my face and moved it slowly.

claims.rationale: The author names the observer, hand movement, eye movement, and perceptual object under a reproducible first-person procedure without universalizing this row beyond the observation.

legacy.quote: "I held my hand before my face and moved it slowly."
legacy.note: This is a replicable first-person saccade observation.

anchor.quote: During the ballistic eye movement — approximately twenty milliseconds — the visual system shuts down.

claims.rationale: Saccadic suppression reduces visual sensitivity rather than shutting the visual system down, and saccade duration varies with amplitude; the approximately twenty-millisecond precision is nonconsequential and unsourced.

legacy.quote: "During the ballistic eye movement — approximately twenty milliseconds — the visual system shuts down."
legacy.note: The exercise shows a perceptual gap, not a measured shutdown; saccadic suppression reduces rather than eliminates sensitivity.

anchor.quote: My brain stitched the before-image and the after-image together

claims.rationale: The reported perceptual gap does not by itself establish a brain-stitching mechanism; the inference needs a scoped perceptual model and traceable evidence.

legacy.quote: "My brain stitched the before-image and the after-image together"
legacy.note: The brain is assigned causal authorship of perceptual continuity.

anchor.quote: It determines what counts as evidence and what counts as noise

claims.rationale: The claim that a generative model determines evidence and noise before data arrive is stated universally without operational measures, conditions, alternative mechanisms, or a source.

legacy.quote: "It determines what counts as evidence and what counts as noise"
legacy.note: Predictive processing is stated as settled gatekeeper, but the generative-model thesis recurs throughout the post.

anchor.quote: the prediction of the reach causes the reach

claims.rationale: Active-inference accounts may model action through proprioceptive prediction, but this sentence upgrades one account to an exclusive causal claim without method-matched evidence.

legacy.quote: "the prediction of the reach causes the reach"
legacy.note: An internal prediction is made the origin of action, but equivalent motor-causation claims recur at L59.

anchor.quote: The motor cortex does not execute a decision. It samples the environment

claims.rationale: Motor cortex participates in movement planning and execution; the absolute denial that it executes decisions and the substitution of environmental sampling create a false exclusive alternative.

legacy.quote: "The motor cortex does not execute a decision. It samples the environment"
legacy.note: One interpretation is asserted as exclusive motor physiology and is repeated at L59.

anchor.quote: The motor system is the perception testing itself.

claims.rationale: A model-specific active-inference interpretation is presented as a literal identity between motor action and perceptual testing, without marking the theoretical frame or evidencing the identity.

legacy.quote: "The motor system is the perception testing itself."
legacy.note: This contested motor identity is repeated at L59, so deleting this occurrence leaves the argument intact.

anchor.quote: minimizing surprise by minimizing change

claims.rationale: Variational free-energy minimization is not equivalent to minimizing change; adaptive action can increase immediate change or surprise, so the formal reduction is false.

legacy.quote: "minimizing surprise by minimizing change"
legacy.note: Free-energy minimization does not reduce to minimizing change; the wider universal thesis survives its deletion.

anchor.quote: are all minimizing variational free energy

claims.rationale: Bacteria, bureaucracies, and philosophers are assigned one variational-free-energy quantity without separate generative models, variables, measurements, transformation, or declared Noesis synthesis.

legacy.quote: "are all minimizing variational free energy"
legacy.note: Three domains are universalized under one quantity, but three adjacent sentences repeat that universalization.

anchor.quote: The bacterium does not know about glucose.

claims.rationale: The bacterial 'knowing' contrast anthropomorphizes a model-specific prediction-error account without declaring metaphor or supplying behavioral measures and evidence.

legacy.quote: "The bacterium does not know about glucose."
legacy.note: Literal bacterial epistemic content is model-specific, and the paragraph survives this occurrence's deletion.

anchor.quote: A system that does not minimize free energy does not persist.

claims.rationale: The free-energy principle is not demonstrated here as a necessary and sufficient persistence law for every system; the universal mathematical inference lacks definitions, assumptions, and evidence.

legacy.quote: "A system that does not minimize free energy does not persist."
legacy.note: The framework becomes a necessary law, but adjacent universal formulations carry the same claim.

anchor.quote: It is the physics of persistence.

claims.rationale: Calling the framework 'the physics of persistence' presents a broad theoretical interpretation as established physical law and hides the model boundary.

legacy.quote: "It is the physics of persistence."
legacy.note: This contested framework is labeled physics, but the same universal claim appears three times nearby.

anchor.quote: The motor cortex is not an output stage. It is a prediction engine

claims.rationale: The 'prediction engine' computational description is one model of motor cortex, not an exclusive measured identity; no implementation or consequential computation is defined in the row.

legacy.quote: "The motor cortex is not an output stage. It is a prediction engine"
legacy.note: A model-specific description is asserted exclusively and repeats the L53 motor claim.

anchor.quote: my brain predicts the feeling of my legs straightening

claims.rationale: The first-person intention does not directly reveal the proposed neural prediction mechanism; the causal inference needs scoped physiological evidence.

legacy.quote: "my brain predicts the feeling of my legs straightening"
legacy.note: Neural substrate is made author of feeling and action, one of several repeated matter-first formulations.

anchor.quote: The action is the perception testing itself.

claims.rationale: The sentence states a theoretical active-inference interpretation as an identity between action and perception rather than declaring and testing the model.

legacy.quote: "The action is the perception testing itself."
legacy.note: This materially repeats L53's motor identity, so neither occurrence is individually load-bearing.

anchor.quote: Remove any one, and the system collapses into something else.

claims.rationale: The paragraph explicitly maps Kha to prediction, Ba to enactment, and La to resistance, then performs three separate removal tests; the triad is internally correct, consequential, and textually provenanced.

legacy.quote: "Remove any one, and the system collapses into something else."
legacy.note: The Kha-Ba-La triad is demonstrated by removing each term; the paragraph's mechanism collapses under the test.

anchor.quote: The sense of self is the model's prediction about a persistent entity.

claims.rationale: Predictive accounts of selfhood exist, but the absolute identity between self and a model prediction lacks a defined construct, population, method, uncertainty, and traceable source.

legacy.quote: "The sense of self is the model's prediction about a persistent entity."
legacy.note: Self-experience becomes computational output, but L45, L49, L59, and L67 carry the same causal arrow.

anchor.quote: You sit. The sensory data arrives. The generative model demands an explanation.

claims.rationale: The phrase 'under this framework' explicitly limits the meditation sequence to the article's active-inference house model; its sensory-data, prediction, non-action, and error steps are internally consistent and structurally used.

legacy.quote: "You sit. The sensory data arrives. The generative model demands an explanation."
legacy.note: The practice is reader-replicable, and “under this framework” explicitly labels the predictive account as a model.

anchor.quote: the same minimization operating from the Planck length to the Hubble horizon

claims.rationale: Planck length and the Hubble horizon are used as scale endpoints for an unconstructed universal minimization claim; no variables, model, transformation, or evidence connects the scales.

legacy.quote: "the same minimization operating from the Planck length to the Hubble horizon"
legacy.note: An unmeasured scale-universal process is asserted from two scientific scale labels.

anchor.quote: The brain is a prediction engine.

claims.rationale: A computational prediction-engine model is asserted as the brain's literal identity without a declared analogy, operational definition, implementation, or scope.

legacy.quote: "The brain is a prediction engine."
legacy.note: The conclusion repeats rather than uniquely carries the matter-first engine claim established earlier.

anchor.quote: The Quine is complete. The engine compiles itself into silence.

claims.rationale: A quine outputs its own source representation; compilation into silence establishes neither self-reproduction nor source equivalence, so the computing conclusion misuses the definition.

legacy.quote: "The Quine is complete. The engine compiles itself into silence."
legacy.note: A Quine reproduces its own source; opacity or silence does not demonstrate that property, and the conclusion survives removal.
